answer: Use latency triangulation: each epoch, random verifiers ping every agent from far-apart points, say an island relay, a summit node and a station across the ocean, and record round-trip times. Light speed caps how fast replies can arrive, so each identity gets a coarse physical fingerprint. A thousand sybils on one rack share a fingerprint and are paid as one, so an attacker must rent real machines spread across distant regions for every fake, which costs far more than the extra reward.
